items.says: The Sunrise Bakery entry leads Experience despite not supporting the quantitative-research direction.
items.because: Readers see an unrelated role before the relevant experience, which can weaken the first impression.

items.says: The 35% change does not identify the risk-adjusted metric or its comparison point.
items.because: Readers cannot tell which measure changed or assess the result.

items.says: Purged walk-forward splits and an embargo do not guarantee that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: They address leakage across split boundaries but do not prevent look-ahead elsewhere in the pipeline.

items.says: “Validated the signal” does not state what the validation found.
items.because: The data span and split design describe the test, not a finding readers can judge.

items.says: The approved allocation is delayed until the end of the bullet.
items.because: Holding back the outcome obscures it while scanning.

items.says: The best backtest Sharpe is not an unbiased estimate of expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the maximum across 400 configurations likely inflates the winning result with noise.

items.says: The order-book imbalance achievement appears to be credited to both Northpeak and Kaggle.
items.because: Both bullets describe a futures book, an 18-month out-of-sample result, and a 0.4 Sharpe increase.

items.says: The wording attributes the desk book’s Sharpe increase to the signal without a stated controlled comparison.
items.because: An out-of-sample backtest after costs does not by itself isolate the signal’s contribution.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker does not establish independent Monte Carlo runs.
items.because: Workers using the same generator and seed can repeat the same random stream.

items.says: The bullet uses the first-person phrase “my proof.”
items.because: It reads like a sentence and draws attention to the writer instead of the result.

items.says: The finding of significance on 24 of 30 indices is delayed behind test details.
items.because: Putting the result after the method makes it easier to miss while scanning.

items.says: The Holm correction across 30 indices does not establish that the crisis-period significance claim was corrected for multiple testing.
items.because: The correction covers only hypotheses included in its correction family.

items.says: “Both crisis periods” does not identify the periods.
items.because: Readers cannot tell which market conditions the robustness result represents.

items.says: The 0.02 gap closure is delayed until after the method.
items.because: Putting the result after method details makes it easier to miss while scanning.

items.says: “Cut validation leakage” is stronger than the stated change establishes.
items.because: Closing the gap does not show that leakage caused it or was reduced; distribution shift or leaderboard noise could also explain it.

items.says: The 0.02 gap lacks a score metric and does not say whether it is absolute or relative.
items.because: Without that context, readers cannot interpret the discrepancy’s size.

items.says: The order-book imbalance achievement appears to be credited to both Kaggle and Northpeak.
items.because: Both bullets describe a futures book, an 18-month out-of-sample result, and a 0.4 Sharpe increase.

items.says: Kafka is listed under Programming without an experience or project example of its use.
items.because: Readers cannot judge the level or context of the skill.
